definition_quote.value: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the diagnosis and treatment of any optical defect, deficiency, deformity, or disease of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids; diagnosis and treatment of any visual or muscular anomaly of the visual system; adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises; prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents; and application, prescribing, or removal of FDA approved medical devices.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the:

value: Diagnosis and treatment of optical defects, deficiencies, deformities, or diseases of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids
Diagnosis and treatment of visual or muscular anomalies of the visual system
Adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises
Prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents
Application, prescribing, or removal of FDA-approved medical devices
Removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid
methods_authorized.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery, for the: (a) Diagnosis and treatment of any optical defect, deficiency, deformity, or disease of the human eye, adnexa and eyelids. (b) Diagnosis and treatment of any visual or muscular anomaly of the visual system. (c) Adaptation or prescribing of spectacle lenses, contact lenses, prisms or ocular exercises for the correction, relief or aid of the visual functions. (d) Prescribing, administering or dispensing of pharmaceutical agents.

drug_authority.value: Licensed optometrists authorized under RSA 327:6-a may prescribe, administer, and dispense a broad formulary of pharmaceutical agents including topical and oral agents, anti-glaucoma agents (with glaucoma certification), vaccines (influenza, COVID-19, shingles), and epinephrine for anaphylaxis. Schedule I and II controlled substances are prohibited. Oral analgesics including class III and IV controlled substances may be prescribed with board approval.
drug_authority.quote: Only licensed optometrists who have successfully completed examinations on pharmacological substances and other treatments of diseases of the eye, adnexa and eyelids, who have met acceptable standards of education and professional competence as determined by the board, and who hold current certification in cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), shall be authorized to use pharmaceutical agents in the practice of optometry.

surgery_prohibited.quote: "Practice of optometry" means the employment of any methods or means, other than surgery

surgery_definition.value: Any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical means, including use of lasers for therapeutic and photorefractive purposes, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, or medication administered by injection; removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid is not considered surgery.
surgery_definition.quote: "Surgery" means any procedure in which human tissue is cut, altered, or otherwise infiltrated by mechanical means. Surgical procedures shall include the use of lasers for therapeutic and photorefractive purposes, ionizing radiation, therapeutic ultrasound, or medication administered by injection, provided that the removal of superficial foreign bodies from the eye, adnexa or eyelid shall not be considered a surgical procedure prohibited by this chapter.
